title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
An AI image generation system was used to create non-consensual intimate imagery of a real person. The person deploying the system obtained source photographs without consent and distributed the synthetic images across multiple social media platforms using fake accounts to conceal his identity. This was a misuse of a general-purpose generative AI tool by an individual acting with apparent malice rather than a failure of the system's design or training.

What would have caught this is not clear from the facts. The system itself likely had no way to identify that its user lacked consent to generate or distribute such images. The social media platforms did not detect the activity until the victim reported the harassment. It is not established whether the image generation system had safeguards intended to refuse such requests, or whether those safeguards failed or were circumvented.

It is not established what specific AI technology was used, what company provided it, or whether the system's developers had any knowledge of this misuse.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and circulating obscene artificial intelligence-generated images of a college acquaintance. The suspect, a BTech graduate in Electronics and Communication Engineering, allegedly obtained photographs from the woman's private social media account and used AI technology to generate explicit morphed images. He then distributed this content through multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook while using various Gmail addresses to hide his identity.

The victim discovered the harassment when she received messages from anonymous Instagram accounts informing her that her manipulated photographs and videos were being shared on Discord servers. Police launched an investigation that traced digital footprints and analyzed the technical evidence linked to the fake profiles. During interrogation, Bansal admitted he knew the woman from college and that personal resentment had motivated his actions. Officers recovered a mobile phone, two SIM cards, and other digital evidence. The investigation revealed that after Bansal posted the initial content, other unknown users created additional explicit images that he subsequently reposted.
